note.summary: This HS305 chunk sets out the formula for calculating taxable amounts on employment-related securities (UMV × (IUP − PCP − OP) − CE) and directs users to specific working sheets (12–19) depending on circumstances: single vs multiple chargeable events, convertible securities, artificially enhanced or reduced market value, restricted securities, risk of forfeiture, disposal for more than market value, and benefits accruing to security holders. It also covers 2015 rule changes for internationally mobile employees (IMEs), explaining treatment of foreign securities income, the remittance basis for pre-6 April 2025 years, and the temporary repatriation facility (TRF) with a 12% charge for income remitted in 2025-26, to be reported via SA109. Where employers have already correctly handled foreign securities income via PAYE/P60, employees generally only need to complete SA101 Additional Information box 1 (page Ai 2) unless using the TRF.

note.summary: HS305 explains how to report tax liabilities arising from employment-related shares and securities in the 'Share schemes' box 1 on page Ai 2 of the SA101 Additional information pages, covering cases not fully taxed under PAYE. It sets out charging rules for Schedule 2 Share Incentive Plans (SIP), dividend shares, Schedule 4 Company Share Option Plans (CSOP), and Schedule 3 SAYE schemes, including exemptions on cessation of employment or option exercise in specified circumstances. It also covers NIC elections/agreements deductible against tax due, and remittance basis complications for securities income arising before 6 April 2025.

note.summary: This chunk explains the employee shareholder employment status (available from 1 September 2013) and how shares awarded under such agreements are taxed. Income tax reliefs and CGT exemption for shares from agreements entered into on or after 1 December 2016 were removed, with transitional rules for some who received mandatory advice on 23 November 2016. Employee shareholders must receive at least £2,000 of shares and are deemed to have paid £2,000 for them; the market value minus this deemed payment is treated as earnings. The shares are employment-related securities under Part 7 ITEPA, potentially triggering Chapter 2 (restricted securities) or Chapter 3 (convertible securities) charges, with references to specific HS305 working sheets for calculations.

note.summary: This chunk details how to calculate taxable amounts for various employment-related securities scenarios on Self Assessment, directing taxpayers to specific working sheets (4-11) in HS305 Working sheets (2026). It covers EMI option exercises (including discounted and post-disqualifying-event cases), assignment/release of options, non-tax-advantaged option exercises, securities acquired as benefits (interest-free loan treatment), securities sold/transferred, free or cheap securities, restricted and convertible securities, and artificially depressed market value securities. It also notes post-acquisition tax charges for restricted/convertible securities acquired on or after 16 April 2003.
